name: Ailit
long_description:
Ailit is building the electric energy system for North American freight rail. Our first product, Superwagon, is a battery wagon designed to power existing diesel-electric locomotives, allowing railroads to electrify the fleets they already own.

Superwagon carries swappable battery packs that supply electricity to the locomotive’s existing electric motors. Discharged packs are exchanged for charged ones along the route and recharged off-board, providing operators with limitless range.

We deliver energy as a service, owning and operating the batteries and swapping sites. Railroads pay for energy with no upfront equipment purchase, with pricing set at 20% below today’s diesel cost.

Founded in Stockholm by Christian Lind and Emil Tagesson, our team is now based in San Francisco. We’re building our first full-scale prototype, and it’s being prepared to move a locomotive on battery power in the coming days.
one_liner: Electrifying North American freight rail with swappable batteries.

question_answers.question: What is the core problem you are solving? Why is this a big problem? What made you decide to work on it?
question_answers.answer:
American freight rail needs a cheaper, practical alternative to diesel. Electric power must match diesel’s power, range and uptime at a lower cost. The energy system has to operate at all times. Trains can never be allowed to stop because power is unavailable.

What drew us to this problem was how well batteries suit long-distance rail, contrary to popular belief. The potential reduction in total cost of ownership is enormous, trains can handle the weight, and diesel-electric locomotives already use electric motors, meaning we can electrify the existing fleet.

That gives us a practical starting point and a path forward: electrify existing locomotives with Superwagon, build out the battery and swapping network, then use that same infrastructure to support the next generation of fully electric, autonomous locomotives.

question_answers.question: What is your long-term vision? If you truly succeed, what will be different about the world?
question_answers.answer:
Everything that can go electric will go electric. Batteries are getting cheaper, and a new generation of companies is building the energy infrastructure to support them. Freight rail should be part of that future.

Our goal is to make diesel economically obsolete in rail.

If we truly succeed, Ailit becomes the primary way America moves goods at scale: a nationwide electric, autonomous freight network that makes moving heavy loads as cheap and efficient as possible. By connecting  mines, mills, factories and ports, we enable them to produce and move more at lower cost, strengthening American industry.

founders.title: Founder/CTO
founders.founder_bio:
Building the battery tender that lets railroads run their existing diesel-electric locomotives on swappable battery power. 

At Candela, I took the world's first battery-electric hydrofoil passenger ferry from prototype through certification, into commercial operation, and series production. Before that: battery team at Koenigsegg, led powertrain & electronics at KTH Formula Student, building in-house electric race cars. MSc Embedded Systems, KTH.

launches.title: Ailit - Electrifying freight rail with swappable batteries 🔋🚂
launches.tagline: Battery power for existing freight locomotives, delivered as a service.
launches.body:
# US freight railroads burn an estimated $15 billion worth of diesel every year. We’re replacing that diesel with swappable batteries.

Our battery packs ride on a tender behind existing diesel-electric locomotives, powering their electric motors so railroads can electrify the fleet they already own. Packs swap in minutes at stops trains already make. **Railroads pay per kWh, \~20% below their diesel-equivalent cost, with no upfront equipment purchase.** 

[Watch our launch video & prototype unveil](https://youtu.be/YWmFuvSQO9w)

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=128405&key=user_uploads/2764007/c3a9b8d2-460a-4285-a038-ac0641343111)

### Why rail?

For freight rail, electrification has to meet a simple requirement: **match diesel’s power, range and uptime at a lower cost.**

What drew us to this problem was how well batteries suit long-distance rail. The potential operating savings are enormous, trains can handle the battery weight, and diesel-electric locomotives already use electric motors. 

This means the existing fleet stands ready to be electrified.

## How it works

Our first product, Superwagon, carries swappable battery packs that supply electricity to the locomotive’s electric traction motors. The diesel engine stays onboard as backup. Discharged packs are exchanged for charged ones and recharged off-board.

We finance and operate the batteries and swapping sites, providing energy to the operators at a discount. **Day-one savings without having to buy or manage battery systems.**

## Team, progress & full-scale prototype

**We’ve completed our first full-scale prototype with a swappable battery pack. It’s now ready to power our first locomotive movements.**

Our team’s experience includes taking the worlds first electric hydro-foiling ferry from prototype to series production at **Candela**, drivetrain development at **Koenigsegg**, and autonomous military drones at **Nautrik**.

![uploaded image](/media/?type=post&id=128405&key=user_uploads/2764007/95f961e2-11fb-450c-b444-e1b4b53aebe4)

**The future is not diesel. We’re building what comes next.**
